title: Fix GitHub Actions shell template injection
description: actionlint and zizmor found direct GitHub expression interpolation inside shell run blocks, notably ci.yml release-please skip logic and release-please shell variables.
design: Pass GitHub context and action outputs through env variables before shell evaluation. Avoid embedding attacker-controllable expressions directly inside run scripts.
acceptance_criteria: actionlint and zizmor no longer report template-injection findings for workflow shell blocks; CI behavior remains equivalent.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Pin all third-party GitHub Actions by SHA
description: zizmor found unpinned action references across workflows. Project policy now requires SHA pinning for all third-party actions, including low-privilege workflows.
design: Replace tag-only action refs with immutable commit SHAs and preserve version comments for human readability. Local actions remain path refs.
acceptance_criteria: zizmor unpinned-uses reports no unpinned third-party actions.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Add security scan gates
description: Security scanning should run both in task pre-pr and scheduled CI.
design: Add Taskfile security:* tasks for dependency audit, secret scan, Python security lint, and GitHub Actions scans. Add scheduled workflow and include aggregate security task in pre-pr.
acceptance_criteria: task security:audit exists and is called by task pre-pr; scheduled Security workflow runs the same aggregate scan; baseline scans pass.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Implement confirmed hardening fixes
description: Fix all confirmed security findings in priority order, preferring root-cause fixes with tests.
design: Prioritize critical/high findings. Add regression tests for behavior changes and avoid unrelated refactors. Split PR only if scope becomes too large.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed critical/high findings are fixed; medium/low findings are fixed or explicitly deferred with gate tasks; targeted tests and final gates pass.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Add repeatable security scanner tasks
description: Evaluate and add task wrappers for dependency, secret, SAST, and GitHub Actions security checks that should run locally, in pre-pr, and in scheduled CI.
design: Prefer task security:* wrappers. Candidate tools: pip-audit, cargo audit/deny, gitleaks or trufflehog, Ruff S or Semgrep, actionlint/zizmor as noise permits.
acceptance_criteria: Security scanners have repeatable Taskfile commands; selected checks are wired into task pre-pr and scheduled CI; noisy or unsuitable checks are documented with rationale.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Audit supply chain and CI security
description: Review GitHub Actions, release automation, dependency management, devcontainer, SBOM/provenance, artifacts, secrets, and permissions.
design: Enforce SHA pinning for third-party actions, least-privilege permissions, scheduled security scans, and safe pull_request_target usage.
acceptance_criteria: Third-party actions are SHA-pinned or justified; workflow permissions and shell inputs are reviewed; confirmed CI/release findings are fixed or tracked.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Audit application security surfaces
description: Review MQTT, schema/ACL, persistence, logging/error publishing, DI, MCP/CLI, and Rust/PyO3 surfaces for confirmed vulnerabilities and hardening gaps.
design: Use deterministic scan output plus adversarial AI/manual review one surface at a time. Confirm every finding with source evidence and a test or verification idea.
acceptance_criteria: Confirmed findings are represented as beads tasks with severity, exploit sketch, affected files, and verification plan; false positives are noted.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Write security threat model and evidence matrix
description: Document assets, trust boundaries, attacker profiles, and a lightweight control/evidence matrix for the audit.
design: Use docs/planning/security-audit-hardening-plan.md as source. Keep the matrix practical: control, surface, evidence, result, finding/task reference.
acceptance_criteria: Threat model and matrix are committed in docs/planning or a security docs location and referenced by findings.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Security audit and hardening
description: Run a full Option A security audit with a light evidence/control matrix, then fix confirmed findings across code, tooling, CI, release, and documentation.
design: Follow docs/planning/security-audit-hardening-plan.md. Use deterministic scanners plus manual and AI-assisted review. Confirm scanner/AI findings before remediation. Prefer one comprehensive PR unless scope grows too large.
acceptance_criteria:
- Threat model and evidence/control matrix exist.
- Baseline security scanners are evaluated and repeatable task wrappers are added where useful.
- Confirmed findings are tracked as beads tasks with severity and evidence.
- Confirmed critical/high findings are fixed before PR.
- Medium/low findings are fixed or explicitly deferred with gate tasks.
- Security scanning runs in both pre-pr and scheduled CI.
- Third-party GitHub Actions are SHA-pinned.
- Relevant docs are hardened.
- Final checks pass before PR.
close_reason: Completed security audit hardening implementation and verified with task pre-pr

title: Bug 2c: skip array-item consumer props from generation and warn
description: An array-of-objects property (events[].title) has no single value; emitting events[0].title is arbitrary. Preferred resolution (maintainer decision): do not emit an entity for an array-item property by default and warn on stderr, mirroring the existing unreachable-consumer warning. This restores 0.6.1 behaviour (no entity) instead of 0.6.2's broken entity.
acceptance_criteria: 1) HA and openHAB generation skip props where is_array_item is True. 2) A stderr warning lists channels carrying array-item consumer() annotations (mirrors _warn_unreachable_consumer_annotations), wired into ha-discovery and openhab CLI commands. 3) bug2.yaml no longer emits the events[].title entity in either generator.

title: Bug 2b: slugify prop_name in _openhab_item_id
description: _openhab_item_id slugifies device but not prop_name, so a flattened name (events[].title) emits an Item ID 'Bug2_Birthday_Events[].Title' — invalid .items DSL. openHAB parses .items as a unit, so one bad Item breaks the whole file. Latent for any non-identifier property name; fix independently.
acceptance_criteria: 1) _openhab_item_id slugifies prop_name (exactly as device). 2) Regression test: every generated openHAB Item ID matches [A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]* grammar. 3) No behaviour change for bare-identifier property names.

title: Bug 2a: carry structural path on PropertySchema; fix nested-object accessors
description: #384 flattens nested/array-item names to parent.child and parent[].child. That label is used verbatim as a data accessor. Carry structural path segments (path: tuple[str,...], is_array_item: bool) on PropertySchema, populated by _expand_property_children/_build_property_schema. HA value_template and openHAB JSONPATH derive the accessor from path segments (each escaped individually), so meta.source -> value_json.meta.source and $.meta.source.
acceptance_criteria: 1) PropertySchema gains path + is_array_item fields (defaults keep top-level props at path=(name,)). 2) _derive_value_template and _jsonpath_selector build dotted accessors from prop.path. 3) Nested-object bug2 case renders value_json.meta.source and JSONPATH $.meta.source. 4) Regression test: every generated value_template renders non-empty against a schema-derived payload instance.

title: Bug 1: make HA component inference direction-aware
description: _infer_component keys on archetype alone, so a send-only (state) channel of a command entity resolves to a writable component (number/select/switch/text) carrying no command_topic. HA rejects it. The _cmd object_id/unique_id suffix is keyed the same way, mislabelling the state entity as a command.
acceptance_criteria: 1) _infer_component receives channel direction and treats direction=='send' exactly as consumer.read_only (read-only sensor/binary_sensor path, before ha.component override). 2) is_command suffix requires channel.direction in ('receive','both'). 3) Regression test: no writable component (number/select/switch/text/light/climate/cover) is ever emitted without command_topic. 4) bug1.yaml repro now yields a bare 'sensor' on object_id display_brightness_percent with no _cmd suffix.

title: Fix two consumer-generation defects reported by cosalette-apps (0.6.2)
description: Downstream bug report (tmp/cosalette-consumer-generation-bugs.md) against 0.6.2. Two independent defects in _schema/_consumer_gen.py and _schema/_loader_helpers.py that produce output HA/openHAB reject or silently ignore, with no generation error. Bug 1: HA component inference ignores channel direction (send-only state channel resolves to a writable component with no command_topic; HA rejects it). Bug 2: flattened nested property names (parent.child, parent[].child) leak verbatim into HA value_templates, openHAB JSONPATH selectors, and openHAB Item IDs, producing blank entities and an unparsable .items file. Both high severity.
close_reason: All child issues (cos-ccv6.1–.4) and follow-up cos-j6o5 completed and closed; both consumer-generation defects fixed and verified.

title: Consumer generator correctness fixes (no new API surface)
description: Overhaul steps 1-3 + zero-new-surface data wins from the proposal. Fixes confidently-wrong offline generator output for every production app. Scope: F5 (route both generators through shared _device_name_from_archetype/_template, delete _device_name_from_address, slugify nested device names); F6 (unwrap anyOf/oneOf null to effective type); F7 (recognise array + read items); F1 (openHAB one Thing per resolved device); F2/F3 (direction-aware openHAB Item/channel identity from one helper, backward-compatible _cmd suffix on command side only); F4 (direction-aware HA object_id/unique_id/topic via _cmd suffix on command entities only, state entities unchanged for backward compat); F8 (openHAB switch on/off); F11 (default HA command_template {"prop": {{ value }}}); F12 (openHAB formatBeforePublish on command channels, drop inbound-only transform); F14 (minimum/maximum/multipleOf -> min/max/step); F15 (select options from enum); F17 (honour read_only); fill (command,string)->text in _HA_COMPONENT_MAP; filter emitted HA keys by target platform. Includes unit tests, docs (schema-enforcement.md), AI help (consumer topic), guidance asset, and what's-new entry.

title: Consumer generator overhaul (ha-discovery / openhab)
description: Umbrella for the cosalette-apps consumer-integration proposal (tmp/cosalette-consumer-integration-proposal.md). Splits into ship-now correctness fixes (no new API surface) and deferred additive-capability work that each needs its own design review / ADR.
close_reason: Epic complete: all 7 child issues (cos-eq7p, cos-hh2j, cos-1ios, cos-fr9s, cos-f3bn, cos-0p16, cos-v0sg.1) closed. Consumer generator overhaul (ha-discovery/openhab) shipped.

title: Packaging + docs + ADR-003 amendment
description: pyproject: add config-yaml extra (pyyaml). ADR-003: add Amendment (Option 2 revisited) section. docs/guides/configuration.md: document config-file source, precedence, secrets-stay-in-env, --config-file. Update assets/guidance/cosalette.instructions.md if warranted.

title: Wire App + CLIs: --config-file, explicit --env-file existence, fail-loud
description: App.__init__ eager construction catches SettingsLoadError beside ValidationError. _cli.py build_cli: add --config-file, change --env-file default to None, explicit-path existence checks, pass _config_file through, catch SettingsLoadError -> EXIT_CONFIG_ERROR. _schema/_cli.py: _ConfigFileOpt + config_file param on check/dump/init. _schema/_cli_helpers.py: thread config_file through _import_schema_app/_resolve_app_settings, catch SettingsLoadError. Unit tests.

title: Core: config-file settings source + SettingsLoadError + Settings hook
description: New _settings/_config_file.py: SettingsLoadError (carries path), suffix dispatch (.toml stdlib tomllib / .yaml,.yml PyYAML optional / .json stdlib), fail-loud on missing explicit path and malformed content, friendly hint when PyYAML missing. Add __init__(_config_file=...) + settings_customise_sources to base Settings with ContextVar plumbing so source order is (init, env, dotenv, config_file, file_secret). config_file read from model_config.get('config_file'), default None. Unit tests.

title: Native config-file settings source (env > file > defaults)
description: Implement the cosalette-apps enhancement proposal (tmp/cosalette-config-file-settings-proposal.md): a subordinate config-file settings source with precedence env > file > defaults. TOML in core (stdlib tomllib), YAML/JSON behind an optional extra. Fail-loud on explicitly-named missing paths and malformed files (SettingsLoadError). New --config-file CLI flag on schema dump/check/init and the app CLI. Amend ADR-003. Opt-in per app via config_file=; defaults to None so existing apps are unaffected.

title: Bounded command queues with declarable backpressure
description: Add maxsize=/backpressure= (reuse BackpressurePolicy) to @app.command and @app.device. Plumb into router per-entity worker queues and the device ctx._command_queue (currently unbounded at _device_context.py:163). Fixes Finding 3a.

title: Per-entity command dispatch tasks in TopicRouter
description: Router owns a per-entity queue + worker task. route() enqueues and returns immediately so the MQTT read loop never awaits user command handlers. FIFO within an entity, concurrent across entities. Add wait_idle() (queue.join) and aclose() (cancel workers). Wire start/drain into lifecycle. Update MockMqttClient/tests for the async dispatch semantics. Fixes Finding 1.

title: Add timeout= to @app.command
description: Add timeout field to _CommandRegistration and @app.command/add_command signature. Apply via asyncio.wait_for in run_command (reuse telemetry semantics; TimeoutError is an Exception so it flows into publish_error_safely). Composes with unavailable_on. Fixes Finding 2.

title: Concurrent per-entity command dispatch (upstream bug)
description: Command handlers are awaited inline on the single MQTT read loop, so one slow/hung handler stalls commands for every entity. No timeout, unbounded ctx.commands() queue, and @app.device command inputs missing from AsyncAPI. Filed upstream from cosalette-apps (wiz2mqtt, 14 WiZ bulbs). See tmp/cosalette-command-dispatch-bug.md.

title: Stop the annotation eval fallback from masking real errors
description:
Why this issue exists:
_injection.py:157 catches every exception raised during annotation evaluation and re-raises it as "has unresolvable annotation ... Ensure the type is imported and available.", discarding the cause with raise ... from None. Real errors are reported as missing imports.

Scope:

- Under from __future__ import annotations, an async Depends() reports a missing import rather than the actual async rejection. The project's own canonical example uses that import (guides/contract-first-route-design.md:70), so this is the common path.
- The same root cause breaks callable-object dependencies: _hint_source_for (_injection.py:90-98) handles functools.partial and classes but not instances with __call__, so getattr(func, "__globals__", {}) is {} — while docs/reference/errors.md:60 explicitly recommends "a class with __call__".
- get_type_hints failure is also silent: _injection.py:261-269 logs at DEBUG and continues with hints = {}.
- Fix: re-raise TypeError from marker construction unchanged, or chain the cause instead of discarding it.
acceptance_criteria:
- An async Depends() under from __future__ import annotations reports the async rejection, not a missing import.
- Exception chaining is preserved rather than dropped with from None.
- Callable-object dependencies resolve their hints, or fail with an accurate message.
- Silent get_type_hints failure is surfaced.
close_reason: Marker-construction errors re-raised verbatim; eval fallback chains its cause; _hint_source_for handles callable instances; get_type_hints failure logged at WARNING

title: Add state_model to @app.stream
description:
Why this issue exists:
state_model is the only contract-metadata field that is runtime load-bearing: it drives TypeAdapter normalisation of published state and raises ReturnValidationError on malformed payloads (_runners/_contracts.py:327-354, called from _telemetry_runner.py:65-67 and _command_runner.py:236). @app.stream publishes state but gets none of that validation.

Scope:

- @app.stream DOES publish to a static retained {app}/{stream}/state topic via the injected DeviceContext (_wiring/_context.py:108-148, _context/_device_context.py:149 and :195-213). That is structurally identical to a telemetry state channel, yet it gets no validation.
- There is no fallback: a stream handler is an async generator yielding None, so get_return_annotation can never supply the type. Explicit state_model is the only route.
- Drift evidence: stream's metadata set was fixed on 2026-04-27 (0eaa52e), when streams had no DeviceContext and could not publish. ADR-045 (380a59e, 2026-05-08) granted publish capability and did not revisit contract metadata.
- The stated exclusion rationale at _schema/_cli.py:222-226 ("streams use dynamic per-sensor topics") cites ADR-033, which contains nothing on the subject, and is contradicted by guides/contract-first-route-design.md:214-231, where an @app.device publishing exclusively via dynamic sub-entity topics still gets a static state channel.
- Requires an ADR-045 amendment; use task adr:create.
acceptance_criteria:
- @app.stream accepts state_model and it drives TypeAdapter normalisation and ReturnValidationError on the static state topic, matching telemetry.
- The stale rationale at _schema/_cli.py:222-226 is corrected or removed.
- An ADR-045 amendment records the change.
- Tests cover valid and malformed stream state payloads.

title: Remove or re-scope the reserved dependencies= parameter
description:
Why this issue exists:
dependencies= appears on Router.__init__, include_router, and all five Router operation decorators, raising NotImplementedError with the message "reserved for the cos-ebc epic and is not yet implemented". cos-ebc CLOSED on 2026-05-09 with 5/5 children complete. The Router file was added on 2026-05-10 (9eba0de), so the parameter shipped one day AFTER the epic it points at completed.

Scope:

- self._dependencies is stored at _router/__init__.py:120 and never read; it is a dead field.
- The surface is asymmetric: dependencies= exists on Router but not App, so @router.command(dependencies=[...]) raises NotImplementedError while @app.command(dependencies=[...]) raises TypeError: unexpected keyword.
- Guards to remove or re-scope: _router/__init__.py:114-119, _router/_telemetry.py:309, _router/_command.py:141, _router/_device.py:127, _router/_stream.py:129, _router/_periodic.py:99, _app/__init__.py:681.
- Pinned by tests at packages/tests/unit/app/test_router_composition.py:104, :258 and :355.
- ADR-044:26 froze the wording, so this needs a superseding ADR; use task adr:create.
acceptance_criteria:
- dependencies= is either implemented, removed, or re-scoped to a live issue, with no dangling reference to a closed epic.
- The dead self._dependencies field is gone or read.
- Router and App behave consistently for the parameter.
- The pinning tests are updated and a superseding ADR records the decision.
close_reason: dependencies= removed from Router.__init__, App.include_router, and the telemetry/command/device/stream/periodic Router decorators; dead Router._dependencies field deleted; pinning tests rewritten to assert TypeError + signature absence with Router/App symmetry coverage; ADR-044 corrective amendment (2026-08-07) records the decision. BREAKING CHANGE shipped in 6d270b1.

title: Fix false manifest claim in shipped AI help content
description:
Why this issue exists:
packages/src/cosalette/_ai_content/_help_extra.py:415 claims the cosalette manifest JSON "is the same structure as cosalette_inspect_app (MCP)". That is false: manifest was rebased onto asyncapi() and the structures differ.

This is source rather than docs, but it is user-facing help text and was found during the documentation audit.

Scope:

- Correct the claim in _help_extra.py so the shipped help text describes the actual relationship between manifest output and the MCP inspect tool.
acceptance_criteria:
- _help_extra.py:415 no longer claims structural equivalence.
- The replacement wording matches what manifest and cosalette_inspect_app actually emit.

title: Epic: Framework API gaps (contract metadata + DI)
description:
Why this issue exists:
A documentation audit surfaced several places where the public API advertises capabilities it does not deliver, or documents behaviour that does not match the implementation. These are separated from the documentation restructure because they need ADR amendments and a different review path.

Scope:

- Close the contract-metadata gaps on @app.stream and @app.periodic: either make the accepted metadata reach a generated artifact, or stop accepting it.
- Add state_model to @app.stream, the one contract field that is runtime load-bearing.
- Remove or re-scope the reserved dependencies= parameter, whose epic closed before the parameter shipped.
- Make dependency-injection diagnostics honest: stop masking real errors behind a generic "unresolvable annotation" message, close the async Depends detection holes, and make unresolved-provider errors actionable.
acceptance_criteria:
- No public decorator accepts a keyword argument that reaches no artifact and no runtime behaviour.
- Contract-metadata behaviour matches what the decorators' docstrings and the docs claim.
- DI errors name the real cause rather than a generic annotation failure.
- ADR amendments are recorded for the frozen wording that changes.
notes: Two of these change frozen ADR wording and need superseding or amending ADRs, via task adr:create: ADR-045 for the @app.stream state_model change, and ADR-044:26 for the reserved dependencies= parameter.
close_reason: All 7 children (cos-v1dj.1-.7) and related issue cos-o6c4 closed. Acceptance criteria verified against code on main: (1) no public decorator accepts inert kwargs — reserved dependencies= removed/re-scoped (#364), stream/periodic contract metadata now reaches generated artifacts (#365); (2) contract-metadata behaviour matches docs/docstrings (#365, #366); (3) DI errors name real causes — annotation-eval fallback no longer masks errors, async Depends detection holes closed, unresolved-provider errors made actionable (#364, #369); (4) ADR amendments recorded for frozen wording changes — ADR-045 (@app.stream state_model) and ADR-044:26 (reserved dependencies= parameter). bd doctor flagged this as a stale complete-but-unclosed molecule (7/7 children complete).

title: Fix three broken internal links
description:
Why this issue exists:
Three internal links point at pages that do not exist. The non-strict docs build exits 0, so they pass CI today.

Scope:

- getting-started/quickstart.md:587 targets ../guides/dependency-injection.md, which never existed. Retarget it to the new dependency-injection concepts page.
- guides/schema-enforcement.md:512 targets ../concepts/coalescing-groups.md. Retarget it to ../concepts/device-archetypes.md#coalescing-groups, or to wherever coalescing lands after the archetype split.
- guides/transport-availability.md:250 targets ../concepts/health-monitoring.md, a stale filename. Retarget it to ../concepts/health-reporting.md#adapter-health-checks; the HealthCheckRunner diagrams are at health-reporting.md:327 and :465.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three links resolve to existing pages and anchors.
- zensical build --strict reports no warnings for these links.

title: Fix the broken lifespan example in the router guide
description:
Why this issue exists:
guides/router-composition.md:336 shows an 8-line lifespan snippet that cannot run. The correct shape appears in ADR-016.

Scope:

- The snippet uses @app.lifespan as a decorator. No such decorator exists; lifespan is an App constructor kwarg, App(lifespan=...), as shown at guides/lifespan.md:37.
- The same snippet has three further defects:
  - missing @asynccontextmanager;
  - return annotation -> None on a function containing yield, which should be -> AsyncIterator[None];
  - ctx.adapter(I2CBusPort, i2c_bus) called as a two-arg setter, when AppContext.adapter is a one-arg getter (_context/_app_context.py:45).
acceptance_criteria:
- The snippet uses App(lifespan=...), is decorated with @asynccontextmanager, is annotated -> AsyncIterator[None], and uses ctx.adapter as a one-arg getter.
- The corrected snippet matches the shape in ADR-016.

title: Sharpen the router concepts/guide split and fix factual errors
description:
Why this issue exists:
concepts/router.md states something that is false, and the router guide demonstrates only a third of the router decorators.

Scope:

- concepts/router.md owns snapshot semantics, why nested routers are unsupported, and app-level versus Router.
- guides/router-composition.md owns the circular-import task and multi-module organisation.
- Fix concepts/router.md:111, which claims Router decorators are "identical to their @app.* equivalents". That is false: Router decorators additionally accept tags= and dependencies=, and Router.react defers state_type validation until include_router time (_router/__init__.py:218-221).
- The guide demonstrates only 2 of the 6 router decorators (telemetry, command). Cover device, stream, periodic and react, or explicitly scope them out.
acceptance_criteria:
- concepts/router.md no longer claims decorator parity and documents the tags=, dependencies= and deferred state_type differences.
- The concept page and the guide each hold only their Diataxis type.
- All six router decorators are either demonstrated or explicitly scoped out in the guide.

title: Document the real contract-metadata matrix
description:
Why this issue exists:
guides/contract-first-route-design.md:20 claims "All three registration decorators" accept contract fields. Contract metadata is actually a five-decorator feature with asymmetric subsets, and some of what is accepted reaches no generated artifact at all.

Scope:

- Document the verified matrix:
  - @app.telemetry, @app.command, @app.device: summary, state_model, payload_model, behavior, effects.
  - @app.stream (_app/_stream.py:35-45): summary, behavior, effects. No state_model, no payload_model.
  - @app.periodic (_app/_periodic.py:29-39): summary and behavior only; effects is absent at the dataclass level too (_runners/_periodic.py:25-38).
  - @app.state, @app.react, @app.on_configure: none. This is principled, since they are DI and lifecycle wiring rather than contract surfaces.
- Document that Router mirrors App plus tags= and dependencies=.
- Document honestly that metadata accepted on stream and periodic currently reaches NO generated artifact: build_app_asyncapi covers telemetry, commands and devices only, and build_registry_snapshot has no streams key. Cross-reference the framework API gap issues.

Dependency: if the issue adding state_model to @app.stream lands, this page needs a follow-up edit.
acceptance_criteria:
- The "All three registration decorators" claim is gone.
- The page documents all five decorators with their exact accepted subsets and names the three decorators that accept none.
- The inert stream/periodic metadata is stated plainly and cross-references the framework API gap issues.
- Router's tags= and dependencies= additions are documented.

title: Create dependency-injection concept page and reference table
description:
Why this issue exists:
Dependency injection has no concept page, its canonical injectable-type table lives on a nav-orphaned page, quickstart.md makes a false claim about caching, and the link quickstart.md offers for further reading has never existed. The rules below are non-obvious and all verified in source.

Scope:

- Create docs/concepts/dependency-injection.md as explanation, plus an injectable-type table under reference/.
- Document resolution rules: resolution is by exact type identity with an issubclass fallback and never by parameter name; generic annotations such as Optional[X] or list[str] are rejected at registration; async dependency callables are rejected (di.py:63-71); param.default is ignored entirely so optional injection is impossible; the registration-time versus dispatch-time error split is deliberate (_injection.py:33-34 defers provider resolution).
- Document marker constraints: Payload() and Topic() are factories used inside Annotated but Message is a bare type annotation, which is asymmetric; the marker must be the FIRST metadata element because _injection.py:183 checks only args[1]; extra markers past the first are silently ignored; Topic() does not validate the inner type.
- Include the per-archetype DI resolution frequency table: commands and reactors resolve per message (_command_runner.py:177); telemetry, periodic, device and stream resolve once per lifetime, outside the run loop (_telemetry_runner.py:188 versus the loop at :209).
- Document silent provider shadowing: _find_subclass_instance (_injection.py:369-380) returns the first issubclass match in dict order.
- Fix the false claim at docs/getting-started/quickstart.md:586 that the framework "caches singleton results". Only the resolution PLAN is cached (lru_cache on _cached_dep_plan, _injection.py:506); dependency callables are invoked on every resolution with no memoization.
- Retarget the dead link at quickstart.md:587 (../guides/dependency-injection.md, which never existed) to the new concepts page.
- Add the dispatch-time DI errors to docs/reference/errors.md, where they are currently absent: "Cannot resolve parameter", "Topic() marker requires a request context", "Message type requires a request context".

Source material: the canonical injectable-type table currently lives in the nav-orphaned docs/reference/cosalette-framework-reference.instructions.md:573.
acceptance_criteria:
- docs/concepts/dependency-injection.md exists, is listed in nav, and explains resolution rules, marker constraints, and provider shadowing.
- A reference page carries the injectable-type table and the per-archetype resolution frequency table.
- quickstart.md no longer claims singleton results are cached and states that only the resolution plan is cached.
- quickstart.md:587 points at a page that exists.
- reference/errors.md lists the three dispatch-time DI errors.

title: Run copier update to v1.19.2
description:
## Command

```
uvx --python 3.14 --with jinja2-time copier update --trust --vcs-ref v1.19.2
```

## New question to answer

`create_remote_repo` is new in v1.19.0 — answer **`false`**.
`repo_visibility` is then skipped automatically by its `when` condition, so it
should not be prompted.

All other answers keep their existing values (including the `surge_token: true`
fix from the previous issue).

## Expected outcome

- 55 conflict hunks across 14 files
- Conflicts are written as **inline conflict markers**
- **No `.rej` files** should be produced

## Acceptance

title: Fix surge_token answer drift (false → true)
description:
## Why (root-cause fix)

`.copier-answers.yml` claims `surge_token: false`, but reality disagrees:
`.github/workflows/docs.yml` is built entirely on `secrets.SURGE_TOKEN` —
surge.sh main deploy, PR preview deploys, and PR preview teardown.

Because the recorded answer is wrong, copier renders the **GitHub Pages**
variant of `docs.yml` on every single update, which guarantees a recurring
5-hunk conflict on a file we always resolve the same way.

Setting the answer to `true` is a root-cause fix that permanently removes this
entire conflict class.

## Ordering

This MUST be done **before** running `copier update` (the next issue), so that
copier renders the correct docs.yml variant in the first place instead of
producing conflicts we then have to hand-resolve.

## Steps

- Edit `.copier-answers.yml`: `surge_token: false` -> `surge_token: true`
- Commit as a standalone fix so the reason is visible in history

## Acceptance

- `.copier-answers.yml` has `surge_token: true`
- Rationale recorded in the commit message
close_reason: surge_token corrected to true in 18d93d0; note: template gates only docs-preview.yml on this answer, docs.yml is unconditionally Pages

title: Pre-work: clean tree and update branch
description:
## Why

`copier update` refuses to run (or produces garbage) on a dirty working tree,
and copier treats **untracked** files as dirty too. The tree must be clean and
on a dedicated branch before the update.

## Steps

1. Commit the currently staged `.beads/issues.jsonl` as its own
   `chore(beads)` commit. It carries 5 new issues: epic `cos-sdne` + its 3
   children, plus bug `cos-8s15`.
2. Move the untracked `TECH_STACK.md` aside temporarily (e.g. into the
   scratchpad). Copier counts untracked files as dirty. It gets restored in the
   final child issue.
3. Create branch `chore/copier-template-v1.19.2`.

## Acceptance

- `git status` reports a completely clean tree (no modified, no untracked)
- Current branch is `chore/copier-template-v1.19.2`
- `TECH_STACK.md` is safely stashed somewhere it will not be lost

title: Copier template update v1.17.0 → v1.19.2
description:
## Problem

The project is generated from the copier template
https://github.com/ff-fab/tmpl_python_project_kickstart and is currently pinned at
`_commit: v1.17.0` (2026-05-03). The template has moved on to `v1.19.2`
(2026-08-01), which is identical to remote HEAD.

Gap to close: 4 releases / 10 commits / 21 generated-project files.

A dry-run simulation of `copier update` produced **55 conflict hunks across 14
files**.

## Guiding principle

Converge back onto the template wherever the local drift has no good cause, so
that future template updates stay cheap. Keep the deliberate,
cosalette-specific divergence (Rust/maturin build, MQTT support, extra security
gates) and document it explicitly so the next update does not have to
re-litigate it.

## Scope

Thirteen ordered child issues, each blocked by the previous one:

1. Pre-work: clean tree and update branch
2. Fix `surge_token` answer drift (false -> true)
3. Run copier update to v1.19.2
4. Converge wholesale onto template (4 files)
5. Hand-resolve `.devcontainer/Dockerfile` + `devcontainer.json`
6. Hand-resolve `pyproject.toml` (floor bumps only)
7. Resolve workflows: pins only, reject structure
8. `Taskfile.yml`: adopt new tasks, keep local security block
9. Reject template changes for `docs.yml`, `renovate.json`, `render_adr.py`
10. Back-port 3 `qa-task.sh` fixes without losing the local superset
11. Remove copier-recreated artifacts
12. Regenerate `uv.lock` and verify
13. Final verification and drift documentation

## Acceptance

- `.copier-answers.yml` shows `_commit: v1.19.2`
- All 55 conflict hunks resolved, no leftover conflict markers, no `.rej` files
- `task pre-pr` green
- Remaining deliberate divergence documented

## Notes

Full simulation analysis lives at `scratchpad/sim-analysis.md` (ephemeral —
not committed, will not survive the session).

title: schema dump/init: fail loudly when a registration still carries a name_spec
description: Step (a) of the epic, and the first thing to do. schema dump (and schema init) must fail loudly when any registration still carries a non-None name_spec, instead of silently emitting a channel named after the handler qualname (_app/_telemetry_validators.py:64-71 feeding _schema/_asyncapi.py:607,653-673). The error message must state that a settings-derived entity set (ADR-023 callable name= NameSpec) cannot be represented in a static schema artifact. This stops shipping phantom discovery entities: velux2mqtt today ships an HA discovery payload with state_topic velux2mqtt/cover_device/state, a topic nothing ever publishes, while every real cover is missing. Small, additive-behaviour-only change to the CLI/dump path (_schema/_cli_helpers.py:48,80). It does not enable discovery for settings-derived apps — it converts a silent wrong answer into a build error; the actual unblock is (c). Evidence: tmp/cosalette-apps-improvement-proposal.md sections 3 and 4(a).

title: Settings-derived entity names cannot reach the static schema artifact (cosalette-apps proposal)
description: Downstream cosalette-apps proposal (tmp/cosalette-apps-improvement-proposal.md, sections 3 and 4). The AsyncAPI/discovery pipeline is import-time and settings-free, while ADR-023 settings-derived entity names (callable name= NameSpec) are bootstrap-time. Settings-derived entity sets therefore cannot be represented in the static schema artifact, and the pipeline fails silently in both directions instead of erroring. Evidence: schema dump resolves the app with a bare importlib.import_module via _import_app (_schema/_cli_helpers.py:48,80) — no settings, no bootstrap; expand_name_specs() has exactly one caller, inside app.run() (_app/_lifecycle.py:201); pre-expansion, a callable-NameSpec registration's reg.name is the handler qualname (_app/_telemetry_validators.py:64-71, "if callable(name): return _callable_qualname(func), name"); build_app_asyncapi() emits reg.name verbatim (_schema/_asyncapi.py:607,653-673) and _schema/ contains no name_spec handling at all. Live impact in cosalette-apps, verified by actually running the generator: velux2mqtt emits exactly one HA discovery payload whose state_topic is velux2mqtt/cover_device/state — a handler-qualname phantom topic nothing publishes — while every real cover is silently missing; caldates2mqtt emits zero payloads. Every app whose discovery works registers under Python literals known at import time; both apps with settings-derived names are broken. Three children in priority order: (a) make schema dump fail loudly on an unexpanded name_spec; (b) fix the schema check / runtime enforcement validation asymmetry; (c) design gate for a settings-aware schema pipeline (deferred, needs ADR).
close_reason: All 3 children (cos-sdne.1/.2/.3) closed; ADR-051 implemented, fail-loud validation and enforcement alignment in place, tests passing at 92.2%/86.8% coverage. Epic complete.

title: Expose consumer error_type_map hook so LEAK-01 redaction can be opted out per exception type
description: cosalette 0.5.6 LEAK-01 hardening made build_error_payload default-deny: any exception type NOT in ErrorPublisher.error_type_map has its message redacted to the class name. But create_services builds the publisher with dict(_FRAMEWORK_ERROR_TYPE_MAP) alone (3 private framework command exceptions) and there is NO consumer-facing way to register app-level exception types into that map. App.__init__/run/decorators take no error_type_map param. Result: domain exceptions with intentionally safe messages are silently redacted, degrading MQTT error diagnostics. ADR-011 already established pluggable error-type mapping as the accepted decision; LEAK-01 inadvertently closed the consumer wiring. Restore a public hook while preserving default-deny. Framework enhancement proposal2 from ff-fab/cosalette-apps.
design: Option A: constructor param App(error_type_map: dict[type[Exception], str] | None = None). Store self._error_type_map; expose read-only .error_type_map property (copy). Thread through _app/_lifecycle.py create_services() call. create_services() merges: {**(error_type_map or {}), **_FRAMEWORK_ERROR_TYPE_MAP} so FRAMEWORK ENTRIES ARE AUTHORITATIVE (framework wins on conflict, silently — framework types are private/unimportable so conflict unreachable). Light validation: keys must be BaseException subclasses (raise TypeError) — loud failure consistent with LEAK-01 spirit. Preserves default-deny; unlisted types still redacted. Amend ADR-011 to document LEAK-01 default-deny + restored consumer hook + merge precedence. Tests: unit (create_services merge + framework-wins + App stores/validates) and integration (end-to-end app-registered exception publishes full message; unregistered redacted).

Makes ADR-048 retained-topic cleanup a zero-config invariant. Follows cosalette 0.5.0.

title: F-1: startup race — health/availability/registry published before MQTT connect, never retried
description: HIGH. On container start the framework publishes retained per-device availability ('online'), the AsyncAPI registry snapshot (<prefix>/_meta/registry), and the initial heartbeat BEFORE MqttClient connects. Each publish raises RuntimeError('MqttClient is not connected') and is swallowed at ERROR. Broker connects ~2s later but failed publishes are not retried, so retained <prefix>/<device>/availability holds only the broker LWT 'offline' — a healthy device advertises offline forever. Root cause: _app/_lifecycle.py _run_async awaits mqtt_client.start() (non-blocking; only spawns _connection_loop) then immediately runs the startup publishes (_wiring.publish_device_availability, publish_registry_snapshot in Phase 2; initial health_reporter.publish_heartbeat in _wiring/_tasks.run_lifespan_and_devices). Real connect + _connected.set() happen later in _mqtt/_client._connection_loop.
design: Add narrow capability protocol MqttConnectAware (add_connect_callback) in _mqtt/__init__.py. MqttClient implements it and invokes registered async callbacks inside _connection_loop right after _connected.set() (guarded per-callback; fire-and-forget). In _run_async, for connect-aware clients register a connect callback that announces availability+registry+heartbeat; SKIP the eager inline startup publishes for connect-aware clients. Non-connect-aware doubles (MockMqttClient/NullMqttClient) keep the inline startup publishes so existing tests are unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: Retained <prefix>/<device>/availability reflects 'online' while the service is up and connected. No 'MqttClient is not connected' ERROR logs are emitted for startup availability/registry/heartbeat publishes against a reachable broker. Existing MockMqttClient-based startup tests still pass. New regression test proves availability/registry/heartbeat are published only after (and on) broker connect.

title: MQTT startup race & reconnect reannounce (airthings2mqtt smoke test)
description:
Smoke test of airthings2mqtt (image 0.1.2 on RPi4/BlueZ, Mosquitto2) found two framework-layer health/availability defects. MqttClient.start() is non-blocking (spawns a background _connection_loop); the broker connects ~2s later. Startup publishes (per-device availability, AsyncAPI registry snapshot, initial heartbeat) run BEFORE connect, raise 'MqttClient is not connected', are swallowed at ERROR, and are never retried. status self-heals via the ~60s heartbeat loop; availability and registry have no periodic/reconnect re-emit, so retained <prefix>/<device>/availability stays at the LWT value 'offline' forever while the service is healthy. Fix: reannounce availability/registry/heartbeat on every MQTT (re)connect via a connect-callback capability; stop emitting startup retained publishes before the broker is connected.

## Context
Source report: cosalette-framework-bugs.md. Tracking jl4-qob.5. Affects any cosalette app publishing retained health/availability at startup.

title: Decide Router API names and compatibility stance
description:
Why this issue exists:
Before implementation starts, freeze the Router and include_router naming, operation metadata fields, prefix semantics, tag behavior, dependency inheritance, and whether app-level decorators remain canonical or compatibility-only.

Scope:
- Compare Router naming against FastAPI APIRouter while keeping MQTT vocabulary clear.
- Decide shared metadata fields for App and Router decorators.
- Decide whether app.telemetry/app.command remain first-class or become thin root-router aliases.
- Decide deprecation or hard-break behavior for incompatible patterns.
design:
## 1. Decision Summary

Introduce a public `Router` class and `App.include_router(...)` method as the standard
composition primitive for multi-module cosalette applications. Naming follows FastAPI's
`APIRouter` / `app.include_router` pattern closely, adapted to MQTT semantics. MQTT-native
operation archetypes (telemetry, command, device, stream, periodic, reactor) are
preserved on `Router` exactly as they exist on `App`. App-level decorators remain
first-class and are not deprecated in this breaking release.

---

## 2. Public Naming and Construction Rules

**Public names (exported from `cosalette`):**

- `cosalette.Router` — the composition primitive (maps to FastAPI's `APIRouter`).
- `App.include_router(router, *, prefix=None, tags=None, dependencies=None, adapters=None)`
  — the inclusion method on `App`.

**Construction:**

```python
router = Router(
    prefix=None,        # str | None — MQTT topic segment, no leading/trailing slash
    tags=None,          # list[str] | None — labels for introspection / AsyncAPI grouping
    dependencies=None,  # list[Depends] | None — reserved; implementation in cos-ebc
    adapters=None,      # dict[type, ...] | None — adapter declarations for this router
)
```

**Naming rationale:** `Router` (not `MQTTRouter`, not `APIRouter`) — short and unambiguous
in context. Mirrors the FastAPI convention without importing HTTP vocabulary. The name
`TopicRouter` is already used internally for MQTT subscription dispatch
(`cosalette._mqtt._router.TopicRouter`) and must not be reused for the public surface.

**Decorator surface on `Router`:**

All operation decorators present on `App` are present on `Router` with identical
signatures and semantics:

- `@router.telemetry(name, *, interval, ...)`
- `@router.command(name, ...)`
- `@router.device(name, ...)`
- `@router.stream(name, ...)`
- `@router.periodic(name, *, interval, ...)`
- `@router.react(state_type)` / `@router.state(...)`

---

## 3. Prefix / Topic Composition Semantics

A prefix is a contiguous MQTT topic segment appended between the app name and the
operation name at include time. Rules:

- Prefix syntax: exactly one MQTT topic segment — a plain string with no `/` character
  and no wildcards (`+`, `#`), validated by the existing `validate_mqtt_name` rules.
  Multi-level prefixes (e.g. `"sensors/room1"`) are not supported; nest namespaces by
  using separate routers with single-segment prefixes.
- Topic construction at bootstrap:
  `{app.name} / {include_prefix} / {router.prefix} / {operation_name}`
  where either or both prefix segments may be absent (no double-slash created).
- When `prefix=None` on both `Router()` and `include_router()`, behavior is identical
  to registering directly on `App`.
- A root operation (`name=None` on the decorator) is preserved under the composed
  prefix; it does not acquire the function name as a segment.
- Prefix resolution is finalized at `include_router()` call time, not at decoration
  time. The `Router` instance stores its own `prefix` but combined resolution is the
  app's responsibility.

**Example:**

```python
sensors = Router(prefix="sensors")

@sensors.telemetry("temperature", interval=30)
async def read_temp() -> dict: ...

app.include_router(sensors)
# → publishes to: {app.name}/sensors/temperature/state
```

---

## 4. Operation Metadata Inheritance

### Tags

Tags are additive. The effective tags for a registered operation are the union of:
1. Tags declared on the operation decorator itself.
2. Tags from `Router(tags=[...])`.
3. Tags from `include_router(..., tags=[...])`.

Duplicates are deduplicated while preserving insertion order
(router constructor first, include_router second, operation last).

### Summary / Description

Operation-level only. Neither `Router` nor `include_router` can set or override
`summary`. Summaries are per-operation metadata and must be set on the decorator.

### Dependencies

The `dependencies=` parameter is **reserved** on both `Router(...)` and
`include_router(...)`. The accumulation order (app-level → router constructor →
include time → operation) is decided here for implementers, but the concrete
`Depends` helper and runtime injection wiring are deferred to cos-ebc.

Accumulation order (innermost wins for override semantics, but cosalette's dependency
model is additive, not override-based):

```
effective_deps = app_deps + router_constructor_deps + include_deps + operation_deps
```

Passing `dependencies=` before cos-ebc ships must raise `NotImplementedError` with a
clear message pointing to the epic.

### Adapter Declarations

Router-level `adapters=` is a `dict[type, ...]` in the same shape as `App(adapters=...)`.
At `include_router()` time, declarations are merged into the app's adapter registry.
Conflicts (same port type with different impl already registered) raise `ValueError` at
include time, not at startup. This gives early feedback without requiring eager adapter
resolution.

---

## 5. Compatibility Stance for App-Level Decorators and Properties

**App-level decorators are first-class, not aliases, and are not deprecated.**

`app.telemetry(...)`, `app.command(...)`, `app.device(...)`, `app.stream(...)`,
`app.periodic(...)`, `app.react(...)` remain the canonical API for single-file or small
apps. They may share implementation internals with `Router` after cos-s2q.3, but their
public call signature does not change.

Small-app pattern (still idiomatic after this change):

```python
app = App("bridge")

@app.telemetry("temp", interval=30)
async def read_temp() -> dict: ...
```

Router-based pattern (new, for multi-module apps):

```python
# sensors.py
router = Router(prefix="sensors")

@router.telemetry("temperature", interval=30)
async def read_temp() -> dict: ...

# main.py
app.include_router(sensors.router)
```

**No deprecation warnings are emitted in this breaking release** for any existing
app-level decorator or property. The compatibility break in this release is additive
(new `Router` public surface); nothing is removed from the app-level API.

---

## 6. Router Composition Behavior

### Nesting

`Router.include_router(sub_router)` is **deferred** from this release. Nested router
composition is a common FastAPI pattern (see `APIRouter.include_router`) but adds
significant prefix-resolution complexity. It is out of scope for cos-s2q and should be
filed as a follow-on task when the base implementation settles.

### Multiple Inclusion

The same `Router` instance **may** be included more than once with different `prefix`
or `tags` values. Each call to `include_router` is an independent snapshot inclusion
with fully resolved metadata. This allows reusing a router module under different
topic namespaces.

### Mutation / Copy Rules (Snapshot Semantics)

`include_router` captures a **snapshot** of the router's registrations at call time.
Subsequent decoration of the router after inclusion does **not** affect registrations
already merged into the app. This is consistent with FastAPI's behavior and avoids
surprising order-dependent effects.

The `Router` instance itself is mutable until included. Decorating after inclusion is
not an error but is silently ignored for already-included operations (the unregistered
operations remain on the router for potential future inclusion).

---

## 7. Stream / Adapter Validation Policy

Current behavior (pre-cos-s2q): `@app.stream` validates adapter compatibility eagerly
at decoration time. This is incompatible with router composition because routers are
typically instantiated before adapters are wired into the app.

**Decided policy (to be implemented in cos-s2q.4):**

- `@router.stream(...)` and `@app.stream(...)` succeed at decoration time even if no
  compatible `StreamablePort[T]` adapter is registered.
- Adapter resolution and stream-type matching moves to application startup (the
  `run()` / `cli()` bootstrap path).
- A pre-flight validation entry point surfaces missing adapter errors before `run()` is
  called, enabling test or CI scenarios that need pre-flight validation without full
  startup. **The public method name and signature are deferred to cos-s2q.4**; do not
  commit to `App.validate()` in this release.
- Error messages must name the missing port type and the stream operation that requires
  it. The diagnostic quality of the current eager check must be preserved or improved.

This is a **breaking change**: apps that relied on `@app.stream` raising `TypeError`
at decoration time for adapter misconfiguration will no longer see that error at import
time. Startup tests that import the app module must invoke the validation entry point
or `app.run()` to trigger the check.

---

## 8. Deferred Work and Boundaries

| Task      | What is decided here | What is deferred |
|-----------|----------------------|------------------|
| cos-s2q.2 | Public names, constructor signature shape, decorator surface parity, snapshot semantics, metadata accumulation rules | Concrete class and include_router implementation |
| cos-s2q.3 | App and Router must share one internal registration model; operation metadata shape must be identical | Shared `_BaseRegistrationMixin` or equivalent refactor |
| cos-s2q.4 | Stream/adapter validation deferred to startup; validation-at-startup policy decided | Lazy adapter resolution implementation, public method name and `validate()` implementation |
| cos-s2q.5 | `cosalette.Router` must be exported from `__all__`; `App.include_router` is part of the public surface | `__all__` update, public-API test additions, migration guard tests |
| cos-ebc   | `dependencies=` parameter is **reserved** on Router and include_router with accumulation order decided; `Depends` helper shape is intentionally unspecified here | `Depends`, `Payload`, `Topic`, `Message` helper implementation; runtime dependency injection wiring |

**Not in scope for the full cos-s2q epic:**
- Nested router composition (`Router.include_router`).
- Per-operation response/payload model validation (cos-ebc).
- AsyncAPI schema generation from router tags/operations (cos-bnq).
- Middleware or lifespan hooks on routers.

---

## 9. Migration / Documentation Implications

- A **migration guide** entry is required (docs/guides/) explaining the router-based
  composition pattern and when to prefer it over app-level decorators.
- The `cosalette.Router` and `App.include_router` must appear in the public API
  reference with full docstrings including parameter descriptions and an MQTT topic
  composition example.
- The getting-started example (`docs/getting-started/`) should remain based on
  app-level decorators (single-file pattern); router composition belongs in an
  intermediate guide.
- **AsyncAPI context:** router `tags=` and operation `tags=` will map to AsyncAPI
  channel tags and operation tags when cos-bnq implements schema generation. Choosing
  consistent, lowercase, hyphen-separated tag strings now avoids a later rename.
- **PEP 593 / `Annotated` note:** The `dependencies=` accumulation design is
  forward-compatible with a future `Annotated[T, Depends(...)]` syntax for handler
  parameters, which mirrors FastAPI's PEP 593 usage. The `Depends` helper in cos-ebc
  should be designed with `Annotated`-based markers in mind even if the initial
  implementation uses positional arguments.

---

## 10. Acceptance Checklist (cos-s2q.1 Criteria)

- [x] Public names are documented: `cosalette.Router`, `App.include_router`.
- [x] Metadata inheritance rules are explicit: tags (additive), summary (per-op only),
      dependencies (reserved, ordered), adapters (merged, conflict-checked).
- [x] Prefix/topic composition rules are specified with an example.
- [x] Compatibility stance is explicit: app-level decorators remain first-class;
      no deprecation in this breaking release.
- [x] Router composition rules are specified: no nesting, multiple inclusion allowed,
      snapshot semantics.
- [x] Stream/adapter validation policy is decided (deferred to startup in cos-s2q.4).
- [x] Dependency helper boundary with cos-ebc is explicit (`dependencies=` reserved).
- [x] Deferred-work table maps each remaining task.
- [x] Implementation can proceed on cos-s2q.2 without unresolved naming questions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Public names and metadata rules are documented in the bead decision notes.
- Compatibility stance for app-level decorators is explicit.
- Implementation tasks can proceed without unresolved naming questions.
notes: Decision-only bead. Implementation starts in cos-s2q.2. The decision is captured inline as the design field; the durable architectural record is ADR-044 (docs/adr/ADR-044-public-router-and-composition-api.md), created under cos-s2q.6. Implementers should read sections 2-7 before starting cos-s2q.2. Dependency helper (Depends) implementation boundary with cos-ebc.4 is explicitly noted in section 8. Cross-references: cos-zo3.3 (cosalette ai guidance topic for Router/include_router) and cos-zo3.6 (parity check: ai prime what's-new entry for Router composition) should be updated once Router implementation is complete in cos-s2q.5.
close_reason: Router API naming and compatibility decision captured in bead design notes

title: Epic: Zensical docs cosalette ai and testing migration
description:
Why this issue exists:
The public API shift only succeeds if Zensical docs, generated templates, packaged cosalette ai guidance, and tests all teach the same concise main.py style. Current docs already promise this direction, but some examples drift from runtime behavior.

Scope:
- Update README, Zensical docs navigation/content, quickstart, guides, reference docs, and packaged cosalette ai help/prime/instructions content to teach Router, typed handlers, dependencies, and canonical AsyncAPI consistently.
- Update MCP/scaffold templates so generated apps use the new declarative style from the start.
- Reshape the public test harness toward a FastAPI TestClient-like workflow for commands, telemetry, and publish assertions.
- Add a migration guide for users moving from app-level decorators and raw payload strings.
- Remove stale docs around outdated transports and mismatched examples.

Design notes:
Zensical site structure and cosalette ai content should be treated as one documentation product, not two independent copies.
acceptance_criteria:
- zensical.toml and docs navigation expose a coherent path from quickstart to concepts, guides, reference, and migration.
- cosalette ai help, prime, packaged guidance, and scaffold templates match the published docs.
- README and quickstart show typed payloads, typed returns, dependencies, Router, and AsyncAPI inspection.
- Test harness examples cover the new handler contract style.
- Migration docs explain breaking changes and mechanical rewrites.
notes:
Documentation gaps from cos-s2q Router PR (keep these in focus for the docs/template/AI-content work):
- Public Router composition API: document `Router(...)`, `@router.device`, `@router.telemetry`, `@router.command`, `@router.periodic`, `@router.stream`, `@router.react`, and `App.include_router(...)` with prefix/tag/adapter composition and snapshot semantics.
- Operation metadata shape: tags now live on registration records and accumulate as router constructor tags -> include_router tags -> operation tags, with first-occurrence dedupe; registry/introspection docs should describe this.
- Stream adapter validation: `@app.stream`/`@router.stream` signatures validate at decoration time, but compatible `StreamablePort[T]` adapters are resolved at startup/runtime so routers can be imported before adapters are wired; docs should show the expected missing-adapter diagnostic and the `app.adapter(StreamablePort[T], Impl)` fix.
- Public API guard: `cosalette.Router` is exported from the public facade and existing app-level decorators remain first-class/additive, not deprecated.
- Follow-up implementation note: cos-4rb is included in the Router PR to DRY the Router.stream registration helper before the docs task starts.
Plan approved 2026-05-10: keep app-level decorators first-class/canonical for tiny apps and quickstart examples; introduce Router as production/multi-module composition pattern. Implement hybrid phased plan in docs/planning/cos-zo3-zensical-ai-testing-migration.md, then validate docs/AI/templates/testing parity before PR.
close_reason: Completed Zensical docs, cosalette AI content, scaffolding templates, testing harness modernization, migration docs, and parity validation

title: Epic: Canonical AsyncAPI introspection
description:
Why this issue exists:
cosalette has several partially overlapping public contract surfaces: registry snapshots, manifest CLI, MCP manifest, and AsyncAPI dump. A FastAPI-like framework needs one canonical introspection source that tooling, docs, MCP, and AI guidance can trust.

Scope:
- Promote AsyncAPI generation to the canonical public contract model for MQTT operations.
- Add or stabilize app.asyncapi() and related schema accessors.
- Enrich AsyncAPI output with channels, operations, messages, payload schemas, tags, device metadata, commands, telemetry, streams, and reactors where applicable.
- Rebase CLI manifest, schema commands, MCP manifest, and AI introspection on the same registry/schema pipeline.
- Add deterministic schema tests and compatibility checks for generated contracts.
acceptance_criteria:
- app.asyncapi() or an equivalent public accessor exposes the canonical contract.
- CLI, MCP, manifest, docs tooling, and AI-facing outputs derive from the same registry/schema data.
- Generated AsyncAPI includes typed payload and response/state schemas from the typed contracts epic.
- Snapshot or golden-file tests protect the contract shape.
- Obsolete or duplicate introspection paths are removed or deprecated with migration notes.
notes: Approved design choices for implementation: app.asyncapi() returns deterministic Python dict only (no public YAML accessor); explicit decorator metadata (payload_model/state_model) wins over inferred annotations for generated documentation schemas; manifest/CLI/MCP public introspection pivots to AsyncAPI rather than keeping manifest JSON as the primary output; generated contracts include x-cosalette-contract-version as a distinct contract-shape version alongside app/framework info.version.
close_reason: Epic complete: canonical AsyncAPI introspection implemented, tested, documented, and validated.

title: Epic: Typed handler contracts and dependencies
description:
Why this issue exists:
The current API stores payload_model and state_model metadata, but command runtime still treats MQTT payloads mostly as raw strings. To deliver a FastAPI-like developer experience, handler signatures and return annotations need to become executable contracts.

Scope:
- Parse command and trigger payloads from type annotations or explicit Payload metadata.
- Validate and serialize handler return values using return annotations or state/response model metadata.
- Introduce public dependency and request binding helpers such as Depends, Payload, Topic, Message, and related typing aliases.
- Clarify signature rules for framework-injected values versus MQTT message data.
- Add precise diagnostics for ambiguous or unsupported handler signatures.
- Cover command, telemetry, triggerable telemetry, device, stream, and reactor handlers where applicable.
acceptance_criteria:
- Typed command payloads are parsed, validated, and passed as models or values rather than raw strings.
- Typed telemetry and command returns are serialized and documented consistently.
- Public dependency helpers are exported and covered by tests.
- Invalid handler signatures fail with actionable errors.
- Existing docs and examples can be migrated mechanically to the new contract model.
close_reason: Typed handler contracts and dependency helpers implemented, documented, tested, and gated

title: Epic: Public router and composition API
description:
Why this issue exists:
cosalette is decorator-first, but app authors cannot compose reusable MQTT modules the way FastAPI users compose APIRouters. This epic introduces a public Router and include_router surface while preserving MQTT-native decorators.

Scope:
- Add a public Router that can register telemetry, command, device, periodic, stream, and reactor operations.
- Add App.include_router() with prefix, tags, shared metadata, dependencies, and adapter declarations.
- Normalize App and Router registrations into one registry model.
- Make adapter and stream validation compatible with import-time router composition.
- Update public exports, public API tests, scaffolds, and registry tests.
acceptance_criteria:
- App authors can define Router instances in separate modules and include them from main.py.
- Router decorators support the same core operation metadata as App decorators.
- include_router can apply shared prefix, tags, dependencies, and adapter metadata.
- Public API and registry tests cover the new composition surface.

title: Define secure authorization model for schema control topics
description:
PR #170 review identified a security design gap in the network-first schema plan: control topics (`cosalette/schema/update`, app schema status, aggregate schema status) are specified without a mandatory authorization boundary.

Before implementing schema reload/status features, define and document a safer design that prevents unauthorized publish/spoof/reload actions on shared brokers.

Scope:
- Define broker ACL requirements for control topics
- Define publisher identity requirements (`who can publish what`)
- Decide whether signed control messages are required in addition to ACLs
- Update planning docs and implementation plan accordingly
- Add acceptance criteria and test strategy for authorization behavior

Trigger:
- Must be resolved before implementation of schema reload signaling / schema status publishing moves from planning to code.
design: Recommended model documented in docs/planning/schema-control-topic-authorization.md. Use broker-enforced authorization with unique principals and narrow ACLs: deploy principal publishes cosalette/schema/update; each app principal publishes only its own {app}/schema/status; monitor principal publishes cosalette/network/schema/status. Signed messages are deferred for v1 because MQTT carries only a reload hint and the authoritative schema is the Ansible-deployed local file.
acceptance_criteria:
- Planning docs define publisher identity and ACL ownership for cosalette/schema/update, {app}/schema/status, and cosalette/network/schema/status
- Design states broker ACLs are mandatory for control topics
- Design states signed control messages are not required in v1 and records when to revisit
- Future implementation includes broker-boundary authorization tests for unauthorized publish attempts
- COS-5hx planning references this authorization model instead of a deferred security gap
notes: Resolved in planning on 2026-04-09 as preparation for COS-5hx. Main plan updated and detailed prep note added in docs/planning/schema-control-topic-authorization.md.
close_reason: Authorization model documented for schema control topics; planning docs, acceptance criteria, and test strategy updated as preparation for COS-5hx.

title: Write adopter migration guide: cosalette-apps framework feature adoption
description:
Write a detailed document for the cosalette-apps monorepo maintainer explaining
what framework features each app could adopt and exactly how to migrate.

## Document location

docs/planning/adopter-migration-guide.md (in the cosalette framework repo)

## Structure

For each of the 8 framework improvements (Epics 1–8), document:

### Per-feature section:
1. **Feature name and cosalette version** — which release includes it
2. **What it replaces** — the current workaround pattern
3. **Which apps benefit** — table of app × feature applicability
4. **Migration steps** — step-by-step code changes with before/after examples
5. **Breaking changes** — any backward-incompatible changes to note
6. **Minimum cosalette version bump** — what to change in each app's pyproject.toml

### Per-app section:
For each of the 6 apps (airthings2mqtt, caldates2mqtt, gas2mqtt, jeelink2mqtt,
velux2mqtt, vito2mqtt), a consolidated checklist of all applicable migrations.

### Feature × App matrix:

| Feature | airthings | caldates | gas | jeelink | velux | vito |
|---------|-----------|----------|-----|---------|-------|------|
| 1. on_configure | ○ | ● | ● | - | ● | - |
| 2a. ctx.commands() | ○ | ● | ● | - | ● | ● |
| 2b. Sub-topic routing | - | - | ○ | - | ● | ● |
| 3. Retry/backoff | ● | ● | ● | - | - | ● |
| 4. Lifespan yield | - | - | ○ | ● | - | ○ |
| 5. Health check | ● | - | - | ● | ● | ● |
| 6. Auto-restart | ● | - | - | ● | ● | ● |
| 7. sleep_until | - | ● | - | - | - | - |
| 8. Sub-entity | - | - | - | ○ | ● | ● |

Legend: ● = direct beneficiary, ○ = potential/future, - = not applicable

### Detailed migration examples (before/after):

**Epic 1 — caldates2mqtt migration:**
Before:
```python
_settings = CalDates2MqttSettings()  # crashes --help
for _cal in _settings.calendars:
    app.add_device(_cal.key, make_calendar_handler(_cal))
```
After:
```python
@app.on_configure
def register_devices(settings: CalDates2MqttSettings) -> None:
    for cal in settings.calendars:
        app.add_device(cal.key, make_calendar_handler(cal))
```

**Epic 2a — vito2mqtt migration (asyncio.Queue → ctx.commands()):**
Before:
```python
command_queue: asyncio.Queue[str] = asyncio.Queue()
@ctx.on_command
async def _handle_command(topic: str, payload: str) -> None:
    await command_queue.put(json.loads(payload).get("action"))
while not ctx.shutdown_requested:
    try:
        action = await asyncio.wait_for(command_queue.get(), timeout=5)
    except TimeoutError:
        continue
```
After:
```python
async for cmd in ctx.commands():
    action = json.loads(cmd.payload).get("action")
    await handle(action)
```

**Epic 2b — velux2mqtt migration (payload multiplexing → sub-topic):**
Before:
```python
@ctx.on_command
async def handle_command(topic: str, payload: str) -> None:
    cal_params = _parse_calibrate(payload)
    if cal_params is not None:
        await _handle_calibration(cal_params)
        return
    command = parse_command(payload)
    await execute(command)
```
After:
```python
@ctx.on_command
async def handle_position(payload: str) -> None:
    command = parse_command(payload)
    await execute(command)

@ctx.on_command("calibrate")
async def handle_calibrate(payload: str) -> None:
    cal_params = json.loads(payload)
    await _handle_calibration(cal_params)
```

**Epic 3 — airthings2mqtt migration (add retry):**
Before:
```python
@app.telemetry("airthings", interval=_poll_interval)
async def _telemetry(reader: AirthingsReaderPort, settings: Airthings2MqttSettings) -> dict[str, object]:
    reading = await reader.read(settings.device_mac)
    return {...}
```
After:
```python
@app.telemetry(
    "airthings", interval=_poll_interval,
    retry=3, retry_on=(BleConnectionError, BleTimeoutError),
)
async def _telemetry(reader: AirthingsReaderPort, settings: Airthings2MqttSettings) -> dict[str, object]:
    reading = await reader.read(settings.device_mac)
    return {...}
```

**Epic 4 — jeelink2mqtt migration (singleton → lifespan yield):**
Before:
```python
_state: SharedState | None = None
def get_state() -> SharedState:
    if _state is None: raise RuntimeError(...)
    return _state

@asynccontextmanager
async def _lifespan(ctx: AppContext) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    global _state
    _state = SharedState(ctx.settings)
    yield
    _state = None
```
After:
```python
@asynccontextmanager
async def _lifespan(ctx: AppContext) -> AsyncIterator[SharedState]:
    state = SharedState(ctx.settings)
    yield state  # auto-registered in DI

@app.telemetry("sensor", interval=60)
```

notes:
## Retry/Backoff (ADR-024) — Adopter Migration Notes

### Apps that benefit
- **airthings2mqtt**: BLE flakiness (25-min interval → seconds recovery with retry=3)
- **caldates2mqtt**: CalDAV unreachable (2-hour interval → quick retry)
- **vito2mqtt**: serial timeouts
- **gas2mqtt**: meter read failures

### Before/After
```python
# BEFORE: Manual retry in handler (fragile, no backoff)
@app.telemetry('sensor', interval=300)
async def sensor():
    for attempt in range(3):
        try:
            return await read_sensor()
        except OSError:
            await asyncio.sleep(2 ** attempt)
    raise RuntimeError('sensor unreachable')

# AFTER: Built-in retry with backoff
@app.telemetry('sensor', interval=300, retry=3)
async def sensor():
    return await read_sensor()
```

### Gotchas
- retry_on defaults to (OSError,) — covers TimeoutError (subclass since PEP 3151)
- ValueError is NOT retried by default (programming bugs should fail fast)
- Retry counter is cumulative across cycles, not reset each cycle
- Circuit breaker is opt-in: CircuitBreaker(threshold=5)
- Retry is NOT available on @app.command or @app.device
## Adapter Health Check (ADR-028) — Adopter Migration Notes

### Apps that benefit
- **airthings2mqtt**: BLE adapter can wedge (BlueZ crash, dongle reset) — health check probes BLE availability
- **jeelink2mqtt**: Serial adapter can hang — health check detects unresponsive USB device
- **velux2mqtt**: KLF200 gateway connection can drop — health check probes reachability
- **vito2mqtt**: Optolink serial adapter can become unresponsive — health check detects hardware issues

### Before/After
```python
# BEFORE: No health monitoring — adapter wedges silently, devices stay 'online'
class BleakAirthingsReader:
    async def read(self, mac: str) -> Reading: ...

# AFTER: Add health_check() method — framework auto-detects via HealthCheckable protocol
class BleakAirthingsReader:
    async def read(self, mac: str) -> Reading: ...

    async def health_check(self) -> bool:
        try:
            scanner = BleakScanner()
            await scanner.discover(timeout=5)
            return True
        except Exception:
            return False
```

### Framework behavior (zero config)
- `HealthCheckable` is a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol — no registration needed
- Framework detects it via `isinstance()` after adapter lifecycle entry
- Default interval: 30 seconds (`App(health_check_interval=30.0)`)
- Timeout per probe: interval / 2 (15s default)
- Failed check → all devices depending on that adapter go `"offline"`
- Recovery → devices return to `"online"`
- Exceptions are caught and treated as failure (no crash risk)

### Gotchas
- health_check() must be truly async — blocking I/O will starve the event loop
- Timeout is interval/2, so a 30s interval gives 15s per probe
- health_check_interval=None disables the feature entirely (not 0)
- Startup check runs BEFORE device tasks — devices can start offline if initial check fails
- Health checks are informational only — telemetry polling continues even when unhealthy
- The adapter-to-device mapping uses DI introspection: only devices that inject the adapter's port type are affected
- AdapterHealthStatus.consecutive_failures is exposed for future auto-restart (Epic 6)
- Log deduplication: first failure = WARNING, consecutive = DEBUG, recovery = INFO

title: Implement retry/backoff in telemetry runner
description:
Add retry parameters to @app.telemetry and implement retry logic in the runner.

## Requirements

1. New parameters on @app.telemetry and app.add_telemetry:
   ```python
   @app.telemetry(
       "sensor", interval=60,
       retry=3,                              # max retry attempts (0 = no retry)
       retry_on=(BleConnectionError,),       # exception types to retry on
   )
   ```

2. Validation:
   - retry must be int >= 0
   - retry_on must be tuple of Exception subclasses
   - If retry > 0 and retry_on is empty, raise ValueError("retry_on required when retry > 0")

3. Retry logic in _telemetry_runner.py:
   ```python
   for attempt in range(1 + device.retry):
       try:
           result = await device.handler(...)
           break
       except device.retry_on as exc:
           if attempt == device.retry:
               raise  # final failure → existing error handling
           delay = 2.0 * (2 ** attempt)  # 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s...
           logger.warning("Retry %d/%d after %s: %s", attempt+1, device.retry, type(exc).__name__, exc)
           await ctx.sleep(delay)  # shutdown-aware
           if ctx.shutdown_requested:
               return
   ```

4. Retry does NOT reset the poll interval timer — the next cycle starts from
   the original schedule, not from retry completion.

- packages/src/cosalette/_registration.py — Add retry, retry_on to TelemetryDevice
- packages/src/cosalette/_telemetry_runner.py — Wrap handler call in retry loop
