title: Per-device interval resolution from config type (v2 dict-name extension)
description:
When name= returns dict[str, T], allow interval= to accept Callable[[T], float]
for per-device interval resolution from the per-device config object.

## Motivation

caldates2mqtt has per-calendar poll intervals (CalendarConfig.poll_interval). With the
v1 dict-name decorator (COS-3cg.6), the handler can access cal.poll_interval for
ctx.sleep(), but @app.telemetry's interval= must be a shared scalar or
Callable[[Settings], float]. This means caldates2mqtt must use @app.device instead of
@app.telemetry to get per-device intervals — losing the declarative simplicity.

Target API:
```python
@app.telemetry(
    name=lambda s: {cal.key: cal for cal in s.calendars},
    interval=lambda cal: cal.poll_interval,  # ← receives CalendarConfig, not Settings
    retry=3,
    retry_on=(CalDavConnectionError,),
)
async def calendar(
    cal: CalendarConfig,
    reader: CalDavPort,
) -> dict[str, object]:
    events = await reader.read_events(url=cal.url, ...)
    return {"events": [...]}
```

This turns a 20-line @app.device + manual loop + ctx.sleep() into a 10-line
@app.telemetry with full framework support (retry, publish strategy, error isolation).

## Prerequisites

- COS-3cg.6 (dict-based multi-device decorator) must be implemented and tested
- COS-me8.2 (retry/backoff) should ideally be merged so the full declarative
  telemetry experience can be validated end-to-end

## Design phase — analysis and user discussion

Before implementing, review the v1 dict-name implementation (COS-3cg.6) and
answer these questions (present findings to user for discussion):

1. **Type annotation inspection approach:**
   The framework must distinguish between:
   - interval=lambda s: s.poll_interval  → Callable[[Settings], float] (shared, existing)
   - interval=lambda cal: cal.poll_interval → Callable[[CalendarConfig], float] (per-device)
   
   Options:
   a. Inspect the callable's __annotations__ / signature for the first parameter type
   b. Use typing.get_type_hints() for forward-reference support
   c. Require an explicit marker: interval=PerDevice(lambda cal: cal.poll_interval)
   d. Infer from arity + name= type: if name returns dict[str, T] and interval
      callable's first param is NOT a Settings subclass, assume per-device
   
   Recommend exploring option (d) first — it's implicit but unambiguous. If the
   first param is a Settings subclass → shared (existing behavior). Otherwise →
   per-device. Fall back to option (c) if annotation inspection proves unreliable.
   
   Present trade-offs to user:
   - Implicit (d): cleaner API, but "magic" — user must understand the inference rule
   - Explicit (c): PerDevice() wrapper is verbose but unambiguous
   - Could the inference fail? E.g., unannotated lambda: lambda cal: cal.poll_interval
     has no annotations → can't inspect → must fall back

2. **Unannotated lambdas:**
   `lambda cal: cal.poll_interval` has NO type annotations. Python doesn't attach
   annotations to lambdas. This is the most common way users will write it.
   
   Options:
   a. Require a proper function with annotations (not a lambda)
   b. Use the PerDevice() marker wrapper: interval=PerDevice(lambda cal: cal.poll_interval)
   c. Infer: if name= is a dict-callable AND interval= is a callable that is NOT
      already known to accept Settings (i.e., it wasn't registered with the
      existing IntervalSpec pattern), try calling it with the dict value first;
      if that fails, fall back to Settings
   d. Convention: if name= returns dict, interval= callable ALWAYS receives per-device
      config (never Settings). Use interval=float for shared intervals.
   
   Option (d) is the simplest and most predictable:
   - name= returns dict + interval= is callable → per-device (receives dict value)
   - name= returns dict + interval= is float → shared
   - name= is str/None + interval= is callable → shared (receives Settings, existing)
   
   This means you CAN'T use Callable[[Settings], float] with dict-name. Is that
   acceptable? It means the interval can't depend on a global setting when using
   dict-name. The workaround is to put the interval in the per-device config.
   
   Present this trade-off to user.

3. **Per-device interval storage:**
   Currently _telemetry_runner.py stores one interval per TelemetryDevice.
   With per-device intervals, each dict-expanded device gets its own interval.
   This is straightforward — the expansion happens at registration time, each
   device is independent.

4. **Interaction with coalescing groups:**
   Groups require all members to share the same interval. Per-device intervals +
   group= is a conflict. Options:
   a. Reject: if name= returns dict AND group= is set AND interval is per-device → error
   b. Allow: group all dict-devices that happen to have the same resolved interval
   → Option (a) is simpler and safer. Present to user.

5. **Interaction with retry (Epic 3):**
   retry= and retry_on= are shared across all dict-expanded devices. This is fine —
   the retry parameters describe the error behavior, not per-device config.
   Could per-device retry be useful? (e.g., flaky sensor gets more retries)
   → Probably not worth the complexity. Note as future consideration.

2. In _wiring.py / _registration.py, when expanding a dict-name:
   - If interval is float → use as-is for all devices
   - If interval is callable AND name is dict → call interval(dict_value) per device
   - If interval is callable AND name is str → call interval(settings) (existing)

3. Store resolved per-device interval in each expanded TelemetryDevice

4. Validation:
   - Per-device interval + group= → ValueError
   - Per-device interval callable raises → clear error with device name context

with per-calendar intervals, replacing the current @app.device + manual loop pattern.

title: Implement SubEntityContext and ctx.sub_entity() context manager
description:
Implement SubEntityContext class and the sub_entity() context manager on DeviceContext.

## Requirements

1. SubEntityContext class:
   ```python
   class SubEntityContext:
       name: str
       _parent: DeviceContext
       
       async def publish_state(self, payload: dict[str, object], *, retain: bool = True) -> None:
           topic = f"{self._parent._prefix}/{self._parent.name}/{self.name}/state"
           await self._parent._mqtt.publish(topic, json.dumps(payload), retain=retain)
       
       async def publish(self, channel: str, payload: str, *, retain: bool = False) -> None:
           topic = f"{self._parent._prefix}/{self._parent.name}/{self.name}/{channel}"
           await self._parent._mqtt.publish(topic, payload, retain=retain)
   ```

2. DeviceContext.sub_entity() async context manager:
   ```python
   @asynccontextmanager
   async def sub_entity(self, name: str) -> AsyncIterator[SubEntityContext]:
       sub = SubEntityContext(name=name, _parent=self)
       avail_topic = f"{self._prefix}/{self.name}/{name}/availability"
       await self._mqtt.publish(avail_topic, "online", retain=True)
       try:
           yield sub
       finally:
           await self._mqtt.publish(avail_topic, "offline", retain=True)
   ```

3. Optional: if Epic 2 is merged, add on_command to SubEntityContext that delegates
   to ctx.on_command(name) for sub-topic routing

4. Export SubEntityContext from cosalette public API

- packages/src/cosalette/__init__.py — Export SubEntityContext

title: ADR: Sub-entity context manager design
description:
Write ADR for sub-entity lifecycle.

## ⚠️ USER INPUT REQUIRED — present these trade-offs before writing the ADR

### Decision 1: Sub-entity command support — tight or loose coupling with Epic 2?
If Epic 2 (sub-topic routing) is merged, sub-entities get command support "for free."
But the implementation depends on Epic 2's design.

| Option | Behavior | Pros | Cons |
|--------|----------|------|------|
| A: Require Epic 2 | sub.on_command() only available if Epic 2 is merged | Clean integration | Hard dependency, delays Epic 8 |
| B: Independent implementation | sub.on_command() subscribes to topic manually | No dependency | Duplicates routing logic from Epic 2 |
| C: Optional integration | sub.on_command() works both with and without Epic 2 | Flexible | More code paths to maintain |

**Recommendation:** Option C — if Epic 2 is available, delegate to its sub-topic
routing. Otherwise, subscribe manually. Feature-detect at runtime:
hasattr(ctx, '_sub_topic_router').
**Ask user:** Is this pragmatic approach acceptable, or should we hard-block on Epic 2?

### Decision 2: Sub-entity lifecycle scope — context manager only or also persistent?
The current proposal uses async with (temporary sub-entity). But some sub-entities
are permanent (e.g., a temperature sensor on a cover device):

| Option | API |
|--------|-----|
| A: Context manager only | async with ctx.sub_entity("cal") as sub: ... |
| B: Context manager + persistent | ctx.add_sub_entity("temp") → always online |
| C: Context manager only, persistent via never-exiting with-block | Workaround |

**Recommendation:** Option A for v1 — context manager only. Persistent sub-entities
are a v2 concern. The workaround (long-running with-block) works.
**Ask user:** Is context-manager-only sufficient for velux2mqtt's calibration and
vito2mqtt's legionella? Both are temporary by nature.

### Decision 3: Sub-entity state topic — retain or not?
When a sub-entity publishes state, should it be retained?
- calibrate/state = {"step": "measuring"} — should this persist after calibration ends?
- If retained, Home Assistant sees stale calibration state after it's done.

**Recommendation:** Retain during sub-entity lifecycle, publish empty/null on
__aexit__ to clear retained message. Or: publish availability "offline" clears
the HA entity automatically.
**Ask user:** What does Home Assistant do when availability goes offline — does it
ignore retained state? If so, just relying on availability is sufficient.

### Decision 4: Sub-entity naming restrictions
- No "/" in name (single level, already decided in Epic 2)
- Should sub-entity name conflict with device name? E.g., device "blind" with
  sub-entity "blind" → {prefix}/blind/blind/state
  
**Recommendation:** Allow it — the topic path makes it unambiguous. But log a
WARNING because it's likely a mistake.
**Ask user:** Any naming convention to enforce?

title: ADR: ctx.sleep_until() design for time-of-day scheduling
description:
Write ADR for ctx.sleep_until().

## ⚠️ USER INPUT REQUIRED — present these trade-offs before writing the ADR

### Decision 1: Default timezone
What happens when tz=None?

| Option | Behavior | Pros | Cons |
|--------|----------|------|------|
| A: UTC | sleep_until(time(6,0)) → 06:00 UTC | Predictable, no DST surprises | Unintuitive for local-time use cases (user thinks "6am" means local) |
| B: Local timezone | Uses system timezone | Intuitive for home automation | Varies by container/host; DST shifts |
| C: Required parameter | tz is mandatory, no default | Forces explicit decision | Verbose for simple cases |

**Recommendation:** Option A (UTC) — predictable and safe. Home automation users
should pass their timezone explicitly: sleep_until(time(6,0), tz=ZoneInfo("Europe/Berlin"))
**Ask user:** Preference? If most cosalette apps run in Docker containers with a
configured TZ, option B (local) might be more ergonomic.

### Decision 2: Multiple daily targets
caldates2mqtt wants "read at 06:00 and 18:00". sleep_until(time) only sleeps until
the next single time. For multiple times:

| Option | API |
|--------|-----|
| A: Call sleep_until twice in sequence | Loop: sleep_until(6:00), read, sleep_until(18:00), read |
| B: sleep_until accepts list | sleep_until([time(6,0), time(18,0)]) → sleeps to nearest |
| C: Single time only | User manages multiple targets in their own loop |

**Recommendation:** Option A or C — keep the API simple (single time). The user's
@app.device loop naturally handles multiple targets:
```python
targets = [time(6, 0), time(18, 0)]
while not ctx.shutdown_requested:
    await read_and_publish()
    next_target = find_next(targets, datetime.now())
    await ctx.sleep_until(next_target, tz=...)
```
**Ask user:** Is a helper function find_next_target() worth including?

### Decision 3: Testability
sleep_until uses wall clock (datetime.now), not the monotonic FakeClock.

| Option | Testing approach |
|--------|-----------------|
| A: Mock datetime.now | Tests patch datetime to control wall clock |
| B: Add WallClockPort | New port protocol for wall clock, FakeWallClock for tests |
| C: Accept limitation | Tests verify ctx.sleep() call with calculated seconds, don't test time math directly |

**Recommendation:** Option C — test the seconds calculation in a pure unit test
(no framework), then trust ctx.sleep() for shutdown awareness (already tested).
Mocking datetime is fragile.
**Ask user:** Is this testing approach acceptable?

## After user approval, write ADR

- packages/src/cosalette/_context.py (DeviceContext.sleep)

title: Implement ctx.sleep_until() on DeviceContext
description:
Implement sleep_until() method on DeviceContext.

## Requirements

1. Method signature:
   ```python
   async def sleep_until(
       self,
       target: datetime.time,
       *,
       tz: datetime.tzinfo | None = None,
   ) -> None:
   ```

2. Implementation:
   ```python
   now = datetime.datetime.now(tz=tz or datetime.timezone.utc)
   target_dt = now.replace(
       hour=target.hour, minute=target.minute,
       second=target.second, microsecond=target.microsecond,
   )
   if target_dt <= now:
       target_dt += datetime.timedelta(days=1)
   seconds = (target_dt - now).total_seconds()
   await self.sleep(seconds)
   ```

3. Shutdown-aware via existing ctx.sleep()
4. Export nothing new — method on existing DeviceContext

title: Epic 7: Scheduled/Cron-Like Device Archetype
description:
Add cron-like scheduling support for telemetry devices, as an alternative to
fixed-interval polling.

## Motivation

caldates2mqtt polls every 2 hours, but calendar data is day-aligned. Events change on
day boundaries, not at fixed intervals. A cron schedule ("0 6,18 * * *") would be more
natural and efficient than 12 polls/day when 2 well-timed polls suffice.

## Scope

### Approach: ctx.sleep_until() primitive (lighter than full cron)

Rather than adding a cron parser dependency and a new schedule= parameter to
@app.telemetry, add a sleep_until() method to DeviceContext. Apps that need
time-of-day alignment use @app.device with ctx.sleep_until().

- ctx.sleep_until(time) on DeviceContext: sleep until the next occurrence of a
  given wall-clock time (datetime.time)
- Shutdown-aware (returns early on shutdown, like ctx.sleep())
- Optional: schedule= parameter on @app.telemetry for cron expressions (v2, deferred)
- ADR, tests, docs

## Why ctx.sleep_until() instead of schedule= cron parameter

1. No cron parser dependency needed
2. Smaller API surface change
3. Composable: apps can combine sleep_until with other logic in @app.device
4. Covers the primary use case (day-aligned polling) without over-engineering
5. Full cron can be added later as schedule= if demand grows

## Apps affected

- caldates2mqtt: day-aligned calendar polling (direct beneficiary)
- Future apps: utility meter daily summaries, weather forecasts

This is harmless in current tests (short intervals, shutdown after 1-2 ticks) but would break multi-tick deterministic test scenarios. Fix: either advance FakeClock inside ctx.sleep(), or base elapsed calculation on time.monotonic()/loop.time(). See PR #62 review comments from Copilot.

May share internal mechanics with OnChange but public API and naming are distinct. Composes with existing strategies via | and &.

title: Include @app.stream in colliding_names() for ADR-019 device/stream name-uniqueness parity
description: Phase 2 review (cos-f4g.4) found colliding_names() in packages/src/cosalette/_registration/_validation.py excludes streams, while the @app.stream decorator checks global registered_names. A stream registered before a same-named device can slip through registration and (after the schema-check stream subtraction) produce a spurious missing_channel over-report. Pre-existing ADR-019 uniqueness gap, non-blocking. Fix: include streams in colliding_names() so device<->stream name collisions are rejected at registration time regardless of order.
acceptance_criteria: Registering a device and stream with the same name raises at registration time regardless of order; test covers both orderings.
